body:
Slice 2 of #4277. Depends on the identity columns.

## Why

Sync today is one-way and one-shot: `createIssues` pushes at publish and nothing ever reads GitHub back. There is no `sync` verb in `bsc plan` (`crates/plandb/src/cli.rs`). Close an issue on github.com and plan.db never learns.

## Shape

**The diff is a separate, pure step from the apply.** The banner (slice 3) must be able to show the user exactly what would change *without writing anything*, and a preview computed by a different code path than the apply is a preview that can lie.

```
bsc plan sync --dry-run [--json]   # compute + report the diff, write nothing
bsc plan sync                      # apply the diff
```

## The four buckets the diff reports

| Bucket | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `completed_local` | plan.db `complete`/`verified`, GitHub still open | close on GitHub |
| `closed_remote` | closed on GitHub, plan.db still open | mark complete locally |
| `new_local` | plan.db row with no `gh_number` | create on GitHub |
| `remote_only` | GitHub issue we did not author | **listed, not adopted** |

`remote_only` stays un-adopted by default deliberately: #738 treats a hand-created issue as untrusted input an agent should not act on, and silently pulling it into plan.db would put it in front of the fleet. It is surfaced in the review so the decision is the user's, not ours.

## Precedence

plan.db wins on **content** (title, body, acceptance, owns, deps — it is the authored record). GitHub wins on **open/closed** (it is where work is actually closed out). The same split `fleetPlanProgress.ts` already encodes: neither source is authoritative alone.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `--dry-run` writes nothing — asserted against a store snapshot before/after.
- [ ] Apply is idempotent: a second run immediately after reports an empty diff.
- [ ] The diff is computed by one function that both the CLI and the UI preview call.
- [ ] A rate-limited / failed GitHub read fails **closed** (report the error, sync nothing) — never a partial apply that reads as complete.
- [ ] `remote_only` is never written to plan.db without an explicit opt-in flag.
